If you wanna appreciate the evolution of the franchise over time, start with Red/ Blue or preferably Yellow, but if you just want all the good stuff then start with Crystal imo. Then Fire red/leaf green (fits nicely with Johto), then Emerald (widely considered one of the best games). Then Platinum, and even though you'll have done crystal I'd say Heartgold/Soulsilver are still worth it, but choose these over crystal if you only want Johto once. Black/White and Black2/White 2 are both good to play as they're direct sequels. Then X/Y which are good but easy (best anime of the series if you care). If you want to see Hoenn in 3d with a better story go for OmegaRuby/AlphaSapphire, but if you don't want to you're not missing tooo much, it's like an enhanced XY set in Hoenn. Then UltraSun/UltraMoon (i played UM but I'd reccomend US as its daytime during actual day time rather than night all the time). Don't bother with Let's go, it's just Kanto again but the game gets simplified a lot and you catch pokemon like in GO (still pretty fun if you wanna play it, nice graphics too). I adored Sword/Shield even if they're not very good games. If you're from the UK like me you'll be able to find a lot of homely charm in some of the places, people and Pokémon inspirations. Brilliant Diamond/Shining Pearl are downgrades from platinum so don't bother. Legends arceus is an absolute must play. Scarlet and violet despite being buggy, half finished messes the story is really good and has a pretty interesting dex of new pokemon. Can't help you with spinoffs though I haven't got into them yet

There are some upgrades in the third installment, but the original games were created as a pair intending you to trade between them to complete their dex. So just use the first 2 if you're running as a pair. The 3rd only really matters for single player viewpoints, like a personal playthrough or a streamer.

Just go with the 2 OG rules to start. Only allowed to catch the first pokemon you see in an area. If a pokemon faints, it's considered dead and must be released or boxed for the remainder of the run. That's all that's required for the run to be considered a nuzlocke. You don't even have to nickname your pokemon if you don't want to.

I've found that hosting Tera Raids helps a lot with the more annoying aspects. If you don't check that you're ready while other people join, you can cancel the raid if someone decides to bring a Moltres to fight a Coalossal. Honestly though I've found that even if one person brings a bad pokemon, if the other 3 pokemon are decent then you still have a good shot in a five star or lower. I've found that going random works sometimes, but sometimes you either end up in a 3 or 4 star raid or you end up looking at a pokemon with a difficult type combination that you lack answers for, and you end up being dead weight.

Naveen is just trying to do his thing despite what his family would want from him, Absol/M-Absol don't really have anything related to that, and M-Absol in specific is noted to be more aggressive/into battling but Naveen doesn't have any "bad side" or anything like that either. ZA's Darkrai kinda just wanted/wants to be left alone, don't think it'd just seek out to join the daughter of Kalos' top celebrity. Also can't just quite reverse the roles of the story since Darkrai's ability produces bad dreams, so that wouldn't really be able to help Ansha at all with what she wants to do.
